extractor_notes: The timecodes are given in HH:MM form only (for example '00:08'), not HH:MM:SS, and the input labels the event list 'indicative'. They are preserved exactly as given rather than padded to seconds or treated as exact. 'CERTIFICATE: BBFC 15 (cinema and home video)' describes one certificate level with two scopes; the schema allows one scope per entry, so it is recorded as two entries at the same rating. 'COUNTRIES: UK, FR' is ambiguous: it may mean the territories of transmission, the countries of production, or the rights territories. I have not used it for production_origin, which is left not_stated, and have flagged the ambiguity of which territory this transmission concerns in not_stated. The THEMES line has no timecode, so o7 and o8 carry timecode not_stated; the description does not say where in the 120 minutes this material falls. The THEMES line partly disagrees with itself as evidence about depiction: it lists 'forced reproduction' and 'captivity' as themes of the work while stating 'No sexual content is depicted'. I have recorded the sexual-slavery material as referenced and not depicted (as the line states) and the captivity and forced-reproduction material separately under human_dignity, without resolving whether the forced-reproduction theme is shown in any form; o7 is medium confidence for that reason. 'is_depicted' is set false for o6 because the input says the impact is 'not shown', although the fall itself is described as occurring on screen; the input does not separate the two clearly. 'is_news_or_current_affairs' is 'no' on the basis of the stated descriptor 'feature film'. 'is_made_primarily_for_children' is not_stated: the description says nothing about intended audience. 'treatment' is recorded as 'fictional' where the only support is that the asset is a feature film; the input describes no scene's visual style, so none is recorded as realistic or stylised.
